newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics to launch broad products.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics to launch broad products.

text.p: Silicon Graphics Inc will launch Monday a widely anticipated set of new products, with computers ranging from entry level desktops for priced at under $6,000 to high-end supercomputers.

Company representatives said the launch, to be made exclusively over Internet's World Wide Web, is Silicon Graphic's broadest in years and will set "new economies" for computing power and performance.
In fact, industry anticipation of the products has been so intense that company executives said last month it was a major factor in forcing them to pare first quarter sales forecasts.

The new lines will include an O2 desktop workstation line which replaces its Indy workstations and which analysts expect will be an aggressive step to battle Microsoft Corp's Windows NT in the lower-end workstation market.

Silicon Graphics is also launching its Origin high- performance enterprise server family, its WebFORCEserver, the Onyx2 high-performance visualisation supercomputers and its Cray Origin 2000 supercomputing servers.

In addition, the Mountain View, Calif., maker of high-end graphics computers and supercomputers plans to unveil its new Scalable, Shared-memory, MultiProcessor (S2MP) underlying architecture for its Origin, WebFORCE and Onyx2 lines.

"Our company philosophy is to 'think outside of the box," and we're illustrating that philosophy today through our new products and innovative use of the Web," Gary Lauer, executive vice president of Silicon Graphics, said in a statement prepared for the launch.

"We strive to put the best, most cutting-edge tools into our customers' hands, enabling them to develop powerful Web applications, process corporate data, solve complex design problems, or create the greatest special effects for the next blockbuster film, better than their competition," he added.
The O2 desktop workstation line is based on its MIPS R5000 and MIPS R10000 processors and provides 10 times more computing power than the Indy, Silicon Graphics said.

The O2 systems are network-ready with Web-browsing and TCP/ IP protocols, includes the new, IRIX 6.3 version of its Unix- based operating system and comes in eight configurations ranging in pricefrom $5,995 for a version equipped with a 180 megahertz (MHz) R5000 to $17,995 for a 175 MHz R10000 model.
Shipped with Insignia SoftWindows, themachines can run a wide range of applications for Windows 3.1 and Windows95.
The S2MP architecture, developed jointly by Silicon Graphics and Cray Research, enables system scalability in a single, 64-bit line ranging from $11,935 to over $1 million.

The Origin servers, which replace the existing line of CHALLENGE servers, can expand from single-processor deskside systems to powerful 128-processor scapable servers without disruptive and costly box-swaps, the company said.

The products include Origin 200 servers with one to four R10000 chips, priced starting at $11,395; Origin2000 servers with one to 64 R10000 processors priced from $29,900; and the Cray Origin supercomputing systems scaling from 65 to 128 R10000 chips and priced from $2 million.
All the Origin systems are binary-compatible with the earlier Silicon Graphics CHALLENGE and POWER CHALLENGE series.

The new Onyx2 family can tackle demanding visual computing challenges from manufacturing through complex simulation and entertainment and carries what Silicon Graphics describes as "a breakthrough entry price" of $80,000 for a one 180 MHz R10000 processor desksite model to $769,000 for its Onyx2 RealityMonster MultiRack with eight MIPS 195 MHz R10000s.

The O2 workstations are bundled with Netscape Communinications Corp's Navigator 3.0 for browsing, electronic mail and news and with Netscape FastTrack Server 2.0 for publishing on the Internet or company Intranets.
An Intranet is a private network with Internet technology.
